items.summary: Added a dated verdict separating active ChatGPT surface failures, resolved cross-provider outages, narrow Grok output failures, and unproven broad capability decline.
Added task-level community reports with source, timing, surface, competing explanations, counterreports, and confidence.
Added fresh audience language, multilingual discovery, and competitor monitoring notes to the private research record.

Updated the verdict after OpenAI, Claude, and Grok incidents resolved: current evidence points to surface, rollout, routing, access, and mixed user signals rather than a proven broad capability decline.
Added a scoped Marginlab Codex time-series result and independent cross-sectional comparisons, with explicit limits against generalizing to consumer chat.
Added field-outcome and monitoring alternatives, including Beyond Benchmarks and current community hubs, to show the gap between lived workflow pain and controlled regression evidence.
Added current provider rollout, access, safety, and model-change context so a day-over-day difference is not mislabeled as capability decline.
Made final served model or fallback, surface, plan, effort, context, and task cost first-class comparison fields when a product can route or switch models.
Added provider-documented safety fallback and plan- or model-dependent allowance as concrete explanations for a worse workflow without a broad capability decline.
Added an unconfirmed Google developer report of a long-context Pro-to-Flash-Lite route switch as a reproducible lead, not a confirmed incident.
Kept the Claude Code tracker’s baseline-collecting state visible and separated field cost signals from controlled regression evidence.

Added a narrow GPT-6 Astra/Codex incident cluster covering false completion, premature turns, safety interruption, orchestration churn, and quota-accounting leads without upgrading it to a core capability verdict.
Added tool execution, final artifact, wall-clock, route, safety-code, and quota fields to the reader method for agent incidents.
Added current field-outcome counterweight and separated rolling outcome data from controlled baselines and issue reports.
Added OpenAI’s resolved usage-limit-reset incident and separated provider confirmation from account-level quota attribution.
Added a fresh Codex desktop WebSocket failure lead and a current ChatGPT shared Project direct-link incident as surface or product evidence, not model decline.
Updated the Astra field counterweight with current outcome, interruption, failed-tool-call, speed, token-cost, and hourly-cost measures while preserving rolling-window limits.
Made capable, available, affordable, and verifiable the reader decision frame and connected fresh quota, transport, multilingual, and observability signals.
Added a new method boundary: a provider-confirmed incident narrows the product lane but does not prove an individual deduction or capability regression.
Added a matched-context Gemini 3.8 tool-selection lead with repeated cells and ablations; kept it explicitly separate from broad capability decline until independently replicated.
Added confirmed Claude Cowork and API surface incidents plus Astra/Codex transport, rate-bucket, official cost, and Fable output-meter evidence to separate usable access from capability.
Made context ablation, repeated tool-call counts, final model identity, and final tool trace first-class fields for a narrow regression diagnostic.
Added Bug Hunt Bench, current rolling field metrics, and tracker states as counterweights while preserving their different estimands and limits.
Added a detailed Gemini Deep Research MCP report with a quoted GCP Support backend explanation; kept the missing tool call and ungrounded final report separate from model-weight decline.
Added a repeated Gemini 3.8 Agentic Video processing-call failure and its tool-loop, structured-output, usage, and prevalence limits.
Added matched public Codex runtime telemetry and current account reports to separate faster step throughput and allowance pressure from answer quality.
Added fresh agent-cost and observability research and made tool lifecycle, final artifact, runtime, and cost per completed outcome explicit reader fields.
Updated the call: real Gemini backend and tool-loop failures plus Claude surface and Codex usable-window signals are current, but broad cross-model core-capability decline remains unproven.

Updated the call: no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven, but Astra monitorability, context sensitivity, Codex intent drift, and account-meter discontinuity are now explicit narrow lanes.
Added OpenAI’s provider-documented Astra monitorability regression and separated oversight visibility from ordinary task quality.
Added a context-audit method for skills, AGENTS.md, prompt pressure, and completion boundaries before attributing early stops or correction failure to model weights.
Added fresh Codex intent-drift and weekly-meter discontinuity reports with explicit independent-replay and server-ledger limits.
Added Terminal-Bench 4.0 as a disclosed cross-sectional counterweight, keeping model-agent-effort and task-set limits visible.
Updated the audience signal: trajectory, user intent, completed outcome, and persistent allowance visibility are the useful unit, not a satisfaction score or token total alone.
Added Artificial Analysis’s mixed Astra-versus-Sol result: broad gains alongside a lower GDPval-AA v2 and presentation-quality slice.
Added Astra-26 evidence that search backend and call budget can swing same-model research outcomes.
Added current Codex capacity, session, and tool-output failure leads and kept them separate from capability claims.
Added a preliminary one-account quota-per-task observatory and the explicit limit that it measures no answer quality.
Added a direct competitor’s live better/worse index and reframed the product as a fast check-in opening into a source-separated receipt.
Added a detailed GPT-5.6 Sol control report showing two exhausted five-hour windows on one unfinished task, separating usable-window economics from an Astra-only capability story.
Added resolved OpenAI Work Mode and GPT-5.6 paid-plan incidents as current availability evidence, explicitly separate from model-quality decline.
Added provider guidance that model, task, context, effort, Fast mode, and multistep work change allowance use; higher effort is not a quality guarantee.
Added fresh community-hub and competitor evidence showing demand for structured incident receipts while keeping sparse participation and attention metrics out of the verdict.
Updated the call: a broken or expensive assembled work system is now better supported than a broad weight decline, while Astra’s mixed benchmark lane remains open.
Added a same-task Astra before/after report after a reported account-capacity throttle, keeping the missing served-model field and small sample beside the sharp output delta.
Added a Codex context-amplification control showing long cached-context behavior across Astra and Sol without turning local telemetry into a quality or quota verdict.
Made requested model, provider-served model, route, capacity state, context, and artifact delta explicit decision-receipt fields.
Updated the status lane with the resolved OpenAI image incident and Anthropic Fable/Mythos incident, separate from quality evidence.
Added fresh community, benchmark, and observability-product research showing demand for reproducible outcome and cost receipts without a prevalence denominator.
Updated the call: a narrow account-capacity-conditioned Astra quality lead is credible enough to investigate, while broad cross-model weight decline remains unproven.
Published the complete 16 September report with the new Astra lead, cross-model context control, status lanes, audience demand, and resolution test.
Added a quantified three-message allowance-drain report and shifted the current lead toward usable-window economics without calling it model degradation.
Added current provider guidance on plan-, model-, workspace-, and fallback-dependent limits as a context lane for account reports.
Added Windows Guardian and sandbox failures as product and execution evidence that can block work before capability is tested.
Kept individual safety disclosures and cross-sectional benchmark boards separate from the standing production-capability question.
Added current community language about capacity shock, usage drain, switching pressure, and the need for a usable-work receipt.
Published the complete 17 September report with the allowance lead, provider rules, surface boundaries, safety and benchmark lanes, and next diagnostic.
Updated the verdict: calm declared status does not clear silent route or task-quality problems; no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.
Added an alert contract requiring a user-visible task symptom, baseline, threshold, evidence receipt, and reversible action before a degradation headline.
Added Anthropic’s historical routing and infrastructure postmortem as a causal precedent that separates real response degradation from a model-weight verdict.
Added current community evidence-intake language and a problem-log baseline pattern while preserving selection and denominator limits.
Added the 242.3-million-token Codex task as a usable-window and safeguard lead, not a core-capability verdict.
Added fresh managed-surface, non-response, and entitlement evidence showing that access can fail before quality can be tested.
Added the recovered Gemini external-URL file-input path as a narrow backend or permission lane.
Added Langfuse and Braintrust as adjacent observability positioning while preserving the distinction between traces and capability evidence.
Published the 19 September report and expanded the decision receipt with task budget, warning, stop, entitlement, and descendant-work fields.

Updated the verdict: recent provider incidents and a concrete Antigravity tool-contract migration show system change, while provider, public-monitor, and community counterweights keep broad capability decline unproven.
Added AI Drift Detector and Pondral as differently scoped public monitors and kept their coding-alert versus search-visibility estimands separate.
Added tool-contract version, migration state, benchmark coverage, and switching reason to the decision receipt method.
Added current Codex quota and cross-provider switching language as audience evidence with explicit self-selection limits.
Kept the broad call at no proven cross-model capability decline while adding current operational status, resolved incident, and causal-attribution limits.
Added a repeated-measurement lane: 31,352 observations across 49 model identifiers show between-day movement larger than within-day variation, without proving a weight change.
Added a narrow GPT-5.6 Sol slowdown, rollback, and mistake report as a replay lead rather than prevalence or capability proof.
Expanded the decision receipt with within-day and between-day variance, configuration, judge or harness, availability coverage, and session continuity.
Published the 21 September report: drift is measurable, but the cause still needs a receipt.
Added Anthropic’s resolved same-day multi-model error incident across Claude surfaces as availability evidence, separate from capability decline.
Added OpenAI’s explicit Chat-only GPT-5.6 Sol update boundary and made product surface part of the comparison identity.
Added current Chat-versus-Work community reports and official paid-account access restrictions as a narrow system-quality and entitlement lane.
Added judge version instability and public-monitor snapshot age to the drift receipt and signal table.
Published the 22 September report: an outage and a surface split sharpen the test, but do not prove broad model decline.
Updated the dated verdict with an OpenAI ChatGPT availability incident, a narrow Chat-versus-Work execution lead, and a positive Astra cross-sectional counterweight.
Added execution class, served-model provenance, task budget, completed artifact, and post-action outcome to the public decision receipt.
Added fresh audience evidence on Chat/Work execution, quota receipts, scope boundaries, model routing, and observability vocabulary.
Published the 23 September report with linked provider, community, evaluation, and observability sources.
Updated the verdict with OpenAI’s official GPT-6 Sol/Luna rollout boundary: Work, Codex, and API changed before ordinary Chat.
Added request, server, native, client, and final model-attribution agreement to the replay receipt after a detailed ChatGPT Web mismatch report.
Added hidden tool/file payload, conversation-capacity, and per-task allowance evidence as usable-work lanes separate from capability decline.
Added Anthropic Opus 5.5, Prompt Drift Lab, and DriftBench as positive or methodological counterweights with explicit scope limits.
Published the 24 September report: the rollout moved before the verdict did.
Added Sonar and PolicyBench counterweights: GPT-6 Sol is above GPT-5.6 Sol on their current suites, with task, effort, serving, and judge limits.
Added a ten-task matched Luna comparison that separates speed from first-pass and review quality instead of treating them as one score.
Added a Codex subscription versus API effort mismatch lead and made route, effort, and served identity part of the next replay.
Separated API token prices from included subscription work, limits, and usable-window value.
Added AI Drift Detector’s fixed weekly evaluator as competitive context and kept its estimand separate from this pool’s surface and action receipt.
Updated the call: independent and matched evidence disagree by task, so no broad decline is proven and a deployed replay is the next test.
Added a negative Bug Hunt coding slice, a near-tied Braintrust API counterweight, and a resolved Codex outage; kept the broad-decline call unproven and made replay fields explicit.
